findings.title: Nil dereference when TopicUser record does not exist during unsubscribe
findings.body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` looks up `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately accesses `tu.notification_level` on line 107 without checking whether `tu` is nil. If a user visits `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` for a topic they have no `TopicUser` row for (or before one has been created), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass` and returns a 500 error. In addition, mutating `tu` directly bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which handles creating missing `TopicUser` records, setting `notifications_changed_at` / `notifications_reason_id`, and publishing changes to MessageBus.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe happens on GET and toggles from regular to muted on repeat visits
findings.body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is routed via `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and immediately modifies the user's notification level on the GET request. Because the logic sets `notification_level` to `regular` when `> regular` and otherwise sets it to `muted`, a second GET request to the same URL (for example, an email client or link scanner prefetching the link before the user clicks it, or the user refreshing the page) will drop the user's notification level from `regular` down to `muted` without their intent.
